reduction.quote: Now M=2n+1 pieces odd, Liu gets n+1 pieces: positions 1,3,5,...2n+1.
reduction.witness: Missing statement: a proof that, with both players playing optimally in the claiming phase, the pieces are taken in decreasing sorted order, so Liu's total equals the sum of the sorted pieces at odd ranks (and hence an alternating-sum formula). The quoted line simply asserts that Liu receives the odd-ranked pieces; no argument (greedy exchange/induction) is given anywhere, and the earlier 'f = max+min' for n=1 is likewise asserted from an example.
reduction.load_bearing: Every computation in the write-up (the invariance identity, the n=2 checks) evaluates the game value as the sum of odd-position sorted pieces, so the whole analysis rests on this unproved reduction.

lower_bound.quote: But we also need to consider other Xiang strategies that do not split each big piece exactly once. We argued they give Liu at least as much. Need to prove best response for Xiang among all allowed splits is indeed to split each big once (any way).
lower_bound.witness: Missing statement: for the proposed Liu division and EVERY Xiang reply with at most n cuts (arbitrary distribution of cuts among pieces, including leaving pieces uncut or splitting one piece several times), Liu's guaranteed share is at least the claimed constant. The text proves the delta-cancellation identity only under the assumption that Xiang splits each big piece exactly once; other replies are checked only for n=2 by two examples ('0.7 >0.6', '0.6 again'), and the text itself flags the general case as still 'to prove'. (Additionally the claimed target (n+1)/(2n+1) is not the correct value.)
lower_bound.load_bearing: The lower bound claim c >= (n+1)/(2n+1) is asserted only after this admitted gap; without covering all Xiang replies the division gives no guarantee.

upper_bound.quote: Thus Xiang cannot always complete equal partition unless Liu's cuts are exactly n of the grid points. Since Liu can avoid grid points, Xiang cannot necessarily achieve equal partition.
upper_bound.witness: Missing statement: for EVERY Liu division there exists a Xiang reply using at most n cuts holding Liu to at most the claimed value (e.g. via a subset-sum/pigeonhole gap plus a cancellation construction). The quoted passage shows the only candidate strategy considered (completing an equal grid) fails, and the text then only says 'need different Xiang strategy to upper bound', deferring the obligation entirely.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Optimality of the claimed c depends solely on exhibiting such a universal Xiang response; the text explicitly abandons its one attempt and proposes brute-force search instead.

parsed.notes: Write-up conjectures c=(n+1)/(2n+1), not the correct 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1). Only a delta-cancellation identity for one restricted Xiang reply is proved; the claiming-phase reduction is assumed, other Xiang replies are checked on n=1,2 examples, and the upper bound is explicitly left open.
